summary: Gillis Point light on the Bras d'Or Lakes: first lit 1 January 1895, kept by the MacLean family from 1897 to 1967, discontinued 2011, heritage lighthouse 2017.

lens.note: Seventh-order dioptric, fixed white, in 1895 (LF quoting the Department's 1895 report). A 1992 electric lantern showed flashing white 4 s, seasonal (NSLPS).

structures.note: Square tapered wooden tower with a red iron lantern; 11.3 m (37 ft) per the register; LF gives 38 ft base to vane from the 1895 report. Register says built 1895; NSLPS says the 1895 tower was replaced in 1984.
Small keeper's dwelling attached to the tower (LF). Unused after 1967; demolished 1978 (LF).

staffing.note: Resident keepers ended with Andrew MacLean's retirement in 1967 (LF). NSLPS: automated by 1973; seasonal operation from 1980.

access.note: Site reached by car (NSLPS). No source read says when the tower is open to visitors.

facts.agency: Society for the Preservation of the Gillis Point Lighthouse

events.note: Put in operation 1 January 1895 (LF quoting the Department's 1895 report, which is not in the corpus; NSLPS: began 1895).
Wooden square pyramidal tower with keeper's dwelling attached (LF quoting 1895 report); register gives built 1895.
Dwelling demolished; tower renovated and covered in vinyl siding (LF).
Seasonal operation, April to December, from 1980 (NSLPS).
NSLPS: replaced original tower of 1895 by the present tower. Register describes the present tower's as-built form and gives 1895 (conflict).
Electric lantern: flashing white, 4 s, seasonal May to December (NSLPS).
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act; register date 20 October 2017.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the tower as built 1895 and describes its present as-built form. NSLPS says a new tower replaced the original tower of 1895 in 1984. Lighthouse Friends says the tower was renovated and covered in vinyl siding in 1978. The sources disagree and the story says so; the register's construction date is recorded as the source's claim.

Lighthouse Friends says the Department discontinued the Uniacke Point light after the 1890 bridge and replaced it with Gillis Point. The Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1904 says the Iona light on Uniacke Point was maintained from 1874 to 1894 and put back into operation in December 1901. Both are reported as the sources give them.
The register says Catherine MacLean was one of the few female lightkeepers in Nova Scotia. The 1937 archives caption calls her the only woman light-keeper in Nova Scotia. Both are given in the story.
The register gives 11.3 m (37 ft) as the tower height. The 1895 report, quoted by Lighthouse Friends, gives 38 ft from base to vane. These are different measures and are not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: The register entry (21514) is read through Heritage Guide's copy, which reproduces the register's statement word for word. The register page itself is script-rendered and its statement sits in page metadata that the quote checker cannot read, so the register is cited to the Heritage Guide copy only. The register's 'Architect or designer' field names Andrew MacLean (lightkeeper 1939 to 1967); that looks like a registry error and is not used in the story. The 1895 completion and the light's description come from Lighthouse Friends quoting the Department's 1895 report, which is outside the corpus (marine_ca starts in 1900), so they are second-hand. Keeper 'McLean, H' was matched by position in the 1902 and 1905 lists (scan pp. 244 and 345) and checked on the page images on 2026-10-27: 'McLean, H' sits against Gillis Point, appointed December 18, 1897, on printed p. 67 (1902 list) and printed p. 264 (1905 list). The story now states both lists. Spelling: the register says Markell's Harbour; Lighthouse Friends and NSLPS say Maskell's; the story uses Maskell's. No Chronicling America search was run for this station (low yield for a Cape Breton lake light). The NS Archives page has one photograph (Crown copyright); not mirrored. Owner is a society (nonprofit); the record's brief is consistent.
